授業概要
身の回りから都市スケールまでの微気候が、放射、伝導、対流、蒸発などの物理過程によってどのように形成され、それが人間の温熱快適性や暑熱リスクにどのような影響を及ぼすかを学ぶ。地表面熱収支、水収支、植生や水面などの比較的単純な地表面から、建物や街路によって構成される複雑な都市表面へと段階的に理解を深める。さらに、人体熱収支に基づく温熱快適性モデル、適応的快適性モデル、屋外温熱環境指標、暑熱ストレス・健康リスク評価について、それぞれの考え方、仮定、適用範囲を学ぶ。授業では基礎的な物理メカニズムを理解するとともに、最新の研究論文を取り上げ、異なるモデルや評価指標が現象のどの側面を表現しているのかを批判的に考察する。
This course introduces the physical mechanisms that govern microclimate from local to urban scales and examines how these environmental conditions affect human thermal comfort and heat-related risk. Starting from fundamental processes such as radiation, conduction, convection, evaporation, and surface energy balance, the course progresses from relatively simple land surfaces, including dry surfaces, water, and vegetation, to the more complex geometry of the urban built environment. It then addresses human thermal response through heat-balance-based comfort models, adaptive comfort approaches, outdoor thermal comfort indices, and heat-stress and health-risk assessment. Recent research papers will be used throughout the course to examine how different models and indicators represent different aspects of physical environments and human responses, with particular attention to their assumptions, applicability, and limitations.

全体の教育目標
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to explain the major physical processes governing microclimate and human thermal environments, relate surface and urban-scale heat and mass transfer processes to human thermal response, and critically interpret different approaches to modeling thermal comfort, heat stress, and heat-health risk. Students will also be able to identify the assumptions, limitations, and appropriate applications of commonly used environmental and human thermal models

4. Human Heat Balance and Indoor Thermal Comfort

6. Heat Stress and Heat-Health Risk
7. Urban Heat Island: Physical Mechanisms and Spatial Scales
